Dear Hiring Manager,

I'd like to be considered for the Environmental Services Supervisor (Nights) role at St. Brigid Medical Center. I already work overnight in a hospital, where I lead a crew of 6 custodians across three patient floors, so the shift and the setting are familiar ground for me. I know what it takes to keep patient areas clean and safe while the rest of the hospital sleeps.

Infection prevention is at the center of my work. I clean and disinfect patient rooms, nurses' stations and restrooms following infection prevention procedures, and I hold the Certified Healthcare Environmental Services Technician (CHEST) credential along with annual bloodborne pathogens training. Before the hospital, I cleaned offices in a four-building office park and classrooms after school hours, so I've seen how different spaces need different care.

Your posting mentions building schedules and covering call-offs. That's part of my week now: I build the weekly schedule for my crew and arrange coverage when someone calls off, which happens 2 or 3 times a month. I know how much a missed shift matters on a night when the floors still need to be ready by morning, and I've learned to fill gaps quickly and calmly.

I would bring steady leadership and careful, standards-based cleaning to your night team. Thank you for your time. I'd welcome the chance to talk about how I can support St. Brigid's patients and staff.

Sincerely,
Denise Okafor
